title: Safety and Efficacy of Synchronized Cardiac Support (SCS) Versus Continuous Flow VA-ECMO in Cardiogenic Shock
official: Safety and Efficacy of Synchronized Cardiac Support (SCS) Versus Continuous Flow VA-ECMO in Cardiogenic Shock: A Randomized-Controlled Pilot Study
summary: This study aims to investigate the efficacy of the Synchronized Cardiac Support treatment with the Novalung ultimate kit SCS in patients with cardiogenic shock in comparison with patients treated with continuous flow VA-ECMO

interventions.name: Synchronized Cardiac Support with the Novalung ultimate kit SCS

criteria:
Given the exploratory nature of this randomized study, no formal sample size calculation for between-group comparisons was performed.

Assuming that about 20% of the patients will not provide serum lactate levels at 8 hours after the start of SCS treatment in the Pulse SE study, a total of 50 patients will be enrolled, with 25 patients per treatment group.

This sample size is considered adequate to allow descriptive and exploratory comparisons within and between treatment groups and to estimate effect sizes for the primary and secondary endpoints which will inform the design and sample size planning of future confirmatory studies.

The patients will be enrolled in 4 study centres across Europe.

Inclusion criteria:

* Informed consent signed and dated by study patient/legal representative or investigator/authorized physician
* Minimum age of 18 years
* Patients in cardiogenic shock, defined as SCAI C OR D, with evidence of hemodynamic compromise and hypoperfusion:
* Hemodynamic compromise (low cardiac output and elevated filling pressures):

  * Cardiac index \< 2.2 l/min/m2 (invasive or non-invasive measurement)
  * Central venous pressure \> 7 mmHg OR pulmonary artery occlusion pressure \> 12 mmHg OR left-ventricular end-diastolic pressure ˃ 12 mmHg OR B-lines on lung ultrasound
* Hypoperfusion:

  * Lactate ≥ 2 mmol/L OR SvO2 \< 65% OR capillary refill time \> 3 s OR pCO2 Gap \> 0.8 kPa (\>6 mmHg)

Exclusion criteria:

* In case of female patients: pregnancy or lactation period (if patient is ≥ 55 years old or have been surgically sterilized, a negative pregnancy test is not required)
* Participation in an interventional clinical study during the preceding 30 days
* Previous participation in the same study
* Age \> 75 years
* Out of hospital cardiac arrest with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) \> 30 min OR non-witnessed cardiac arrest or no flow time \> 5 min
* Non-cardiogenic causes of shock (sepsis, hypovolemia, etc.)
* Bradycardia or tachycardia as a cause of shock
* Fever (Body temperature \> 38.0 °C) or other evidence of sepsis
* Onset of cardiogenic shock \> 4 h before enrolment
* Lactate \> 16 mmol/L
* Severe peripheral arterial occlusive disease precluding insertion of femoral arterial or venous catheters
* Contraindications for anticoagulation
* Planned use of primary unloading or venting devices at randomization (e.g. Impella or IABP)
* Contraindication for VA-ECMO, e.g. severe aortic regurgitation, aortic dissection, limited life expectation
